key_insight: Reconstruct, Practice, Go Real (RPG) lets embodied agents improve robot execution skills without retraining model weights. It discovers what the robot can already do from offline data, turns those capabilities into simulation practice, and then transfers the improved behavior back to real-world execution.
problem_solved: Robots need reliable performance across many manipulation tasks, but building those skills usually requires heavy human effort for data collection, reward design, and integrating perception with control. This paper tackles how to autonomously improve embodied agents without expensive model updates.
method: Reconstruct capabilities from offline datasets to identify manipulation skills the robot already possesses.
Generate related practice tasks in simulation so the agent can refine execution in a controlled environment.
Use execution feedback and privileged simulation signals during practice, then apply the improved policy/execution behavior in the real world without changing model weights.
impact: This is useful for practitioners because it offers a scalable way to improve robot performance without the cost and fragility of repeated retraining. It can reduce reliance on manual reward engineering and make embodied systems easier to maintain across tasks.
